chunks: Al-Ḥalabī narrated from him, عليه السلام, that he said:

If you do not know whether you prayed four or five, or whether you added or omitted something, then perform the tashahhud, say the salam, and perform the two sajdahs of sahw without bowing and without recitation; you make in them a light tashahhud.

key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed for forgetfulness in prayer
key_terms.سَلِّمْ: give the salam ending the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should one do in salat if unsure whether four or five rak'ahs were prayed or something was added or omitted?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who becomes uncertain in salat about whether an extra unit was performed or something was added or omitted. It instructs the person to conclude the prayer and then perform the two sajdahs of sahw with a brief tashahhud and without ruku' or recitation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1019 - Al-Halabi narrated from him (the Prophet (as)) that He said:

“If you are unsure whether you prayed four or five rak'ahs, or whether you added or omitted something, then perform the tashahhud (testification of faith), say salaam (greeting of peace), and prostrate two prostrations of forgetfulness without bowing or reciting (in them), and you will make a brief tashahhud in both of them.”
